name: CRAFT
operator: Emergence AI (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Emergence AI's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Enterprise platform of agents over company data, composed of Assess and Enrich modules (Toolkit planned), with solutions for Data Insights (talk-to-data), Data Governance and Semiconductor analytics; exposes a hosted MCP server that outside agents can call, and uses A2A between its own agents.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. From the studio's Web Summit 2026 agents list. Pages that describe target architecture or planned features are not counted.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

Autonomy 3 and 4 rest on exactly these two answers and nothing else, both taken from release-note bullets about Data Governance workflows (2026.03 and 2026.04 in the releases page). The I18 span says results apply at once 'since these are read-only analyses', and the same bullet says generated tags and rules still need a reviewer; the I08 span says results are written directly when the workflow finishes. What is documented is that read-only analysis results are stored without approval and that writes of tags and rules wait for a person. No page read shows an agent changing anything in a customer system: execute_query is SELECT only, the MCP tools are read tools, the Operator role cannot create or delete. Whether this is 'works independently, person approves critical decisions only' (I18) or 'agent suggests, person approves each action' (I16) is a reading; the notes should say that the evidence is scoped to the Data Governance workflows and to analysis results, and the card text for Autonomy should not read wider than that. I23.n: The admin guide lists project roles (Owner, Admin, Developer, Operator, Viewer) and what each may do; the MCP page also lists the tools by name.
I23.span: Read resources and trigger workflows. Cannot create or delete resources.

I25.n: The MCP page says the X-Project-ID header selects a project but grants no access, that project membership is checked server side against the caller's token, and that each project keeps an allowlist of the tools each agent identity may call, refusing others with tool_not_allowed; execute_query accepts SELECT statements only, and only this page states the allowlist as current.
I25.span: project membership is enforced server-side against your JWT's claims

I26.n: Background workers, schedulers and automated pipelines (such as the data-readiness workflows) authenticate as service accounts with their own machine identity; the page does not say the chat agents do, which call the platform with the user's token.
I26.span: authenticate with CRAFT using machine identity

I29.n: The platform includes an agent registry for A2A Agent Cards, marked available now, with create, list, update and delete through its API.
I29.span: Unified registry for discovering, managing, and monitoring A2A agents

I38.n: The release notes (2026.03) say generated data quality tags and rules are previewed, with their SQL and validation status, and a reviewer approves them before they are persisted.

I39.n: The API documents a call that cancels a running agent task by sending A2A tasks/cancel to the orchestrator.

I41.n: The audit log records agent tool calls when agent audit is turned on for a project; the MCP page says every call through its tool gateway, allowed or denied, writes an audit event.
I41.span: Agent tool calls (when agent audit is enabled for a project)

I42.n: The admin guide calls the audit log tamper-evident, without naming a mechanism, and gives a 90-day default retention that can be adjusted.
I42.span: The audit log is a tamper-evident record of significant actions

I45.n: The authorization page says permission checks run in the platform services, against OpenFGA, on every API endpoint; the Data Insights overview page adds that its agents call the platform with the caller's token and do no permission checks of their own, and the MCP page that the gateway rejects non-SELECT SQL.
I45.span: All API endpoints use the `require_permission()` dependency to enforce authorization

I48.n: Authorization is an OpenFGA model, written in its DSL and compiled to JSON that the Governance service reads, with relationship tuples checked on each request.
I48.span: Tuples are stored in OpenFGA and queried during permission checks.

I57.n: The Talk to Data API takes a user's feedback rating on each answer turn.

I58.n: The security docs describe four classification levels for the data the platform processes and the handling for each.
I58.span: CRAFT classifies all data processed by the platform into defined sensitivity levels

I61.n: The introduction names the third-party components (Keycloak, OpenFGA, Prefect, LiteLLM) and says models are reached through LiteLLM, naming Gemini, GPT and Claude in an open list.
I61.span: via LiteLLM (Gemini, GPT, Claude, and more)

I68.n: The release notes state a monthly release cycle with calendar versions.
I68.span: CRAFT ships on a monthly cadence using

S3.n: The documentation site serves an llms.txt index whose OpenAPI Specs section links eight OpenAPI descriptions; the file resolved on a read-only fetch on 2026-11-11.

S4.n: The documentation publishes a hosted MCP server that outside agents and IDE clients can call, with OAuth 2.0 PKCE; the endpoint did not answer our read-only probe.
S4.span: external agents to CRAFT's tool gateway over the Model Context Protocol

not_credited.what: I12: several agents coordinate, each with its own context and authority
not_credited.why: The Data Insights agents (Insights, Text2SQL, Coding) are separate services that pass work over A2A, but they call the platform with the caller's token and make no permission checks of their own, so they share one authority; the scope of I12 asks for each agent's own authority.

not_credited.what: S4 through A2A: an A2A endpoint that an outside agent can call
not_credited.why: Agent Cards are documented for discovery by the Talk2Data service and the Insights agent inside Data Insights; no page read documents an A2A endpoint for outside agents. S4 rests on the MCP server only.

The Data Governance workflows page says approving (Save) a profiling or enrichment run is what applies its changes; so a person still approves those runs, and only the three read-only assessment workflows write without approval.
